entries.api: rclcppyy.enable_cpp_acceleration() before rclpy/message imports
entries.notes: Preserves stock node, context, executor, message, and entity identity; completes a same-handle C++ serialized publish to a stock subscription and reports both routes.

entries.api: RCLCPPYY_ENABLE_HOOK=1 with an installed startup hook
entries.notes: A fresh interpreter proves startup activation and the C++ publisher route. Node identity remains stock, while executor and Future wrappers preserve stock call signatures and report Python authority.

entries.api: Installed startup hook with RCLCPPYY_ENABLE_HOOK unset or not 1
entries.notes: Fresh interpreters remain on unmodified stock behavior.

entries.api: enable_cpp_acceleration() after rclpy or message modules are imported
entries.notes: The original Node, Publisher, executor, Future, LifecycleNode, ActionClient, and ActionServer classes are patched in place and message classes are not replaced. Function aliases captured from the rclpy module before activation retain stock behavior but are not instrumented; overridden subclass methods remain user-owned.

entries.api: rclpy.create_node()
entries.notes: Returns the exact stock Node. The custom Context, namespace, remaps, parameters, graph identity, and teardown are covered by the differential contract.

entries.api: rclcppyy.Node(name)
entries.notes: Direct construction and get_name are tested; broader Node behavior is covered by individual entries.

entries.api: Node name/namespace and endpoint identity observed through the ROS graph
entries.notes: Activated and stock scenarios expose the same single requested node and endpoint identity; no companion node is created.

entries.api: Existing subclasses of a Node alias imported before activation
entries.notes: The application corpus constructs an exact pre-activation subclass, preserves its base and Context, and exercises inherited routed methods. Methods explicitly overridden by an application remain application-owned.

entries.api: Generated .msg class imported after activation
entries.notes: Generated message classes remain the original Python classes with unchanged identity and constructor behavior in compatible mode.

entries.api: Nested messages and primitive sequences on the unpatched-message native rclcpp path
entries.notes: The reusable native path has recursive conversion and sequence coverage; transparent import-hook identity for these shapes is not implied.

entries.api: Generated service and action class import redirection
entries.notes: Compatible mode does not redirect generated imports. One source-built nested message/service/action package is proven with stock generated classes and behavior, but broader generated interface shapes are not implied.

entries.api: Node.create_publisher(message_type, topic, depth_or_qos)
entries.notes: Creation, QoS ownership, graph endpoint, and destruction remain stock; publish uses C++ serialization over the same native handle and completes an ordered round trip.

entries.api: Publisher callback_group, event_callbacks, qos_overriding_options, and publisher_class
entries.notes: The application corpus covers a custom publisher class, callback group, explicit QoS, an empty QoS override set, and a live incompatible-QoS event callback. Other event kinds and non-empty overrides remain open.

entries.api: Node.create_subscription(message_type, topic, callback, depth_or_qos)
entries.notes: The complete subscription entity and Python callback dispatch remain stock; ordered delivery and visible backend fallback are covered.

entries.api: Subscription callback_group, event_callbacks, qos_overriding_options, raw mode, and content filters
entries.notes: The application corpus covers callback groups, explicit QoS, empty overrides, serialized raw delivery with deserialization parity, and a live incompatible-QoS event callback. Active filters, other event kinds, and non-empty overrides remain open.

entries.api: Node.create_timer(period, Python callback)
entries.notes: Stock timer authority is explicit. The corpus covers callback groups, autostart=false, reset, callback execution, cancellation, exception propagation, and destruction; required_cpp rejects before creation.

entries.api: rclpy.spin(accelerated_node)
entries.notes: The stock executor remains authoritative and is reported as Python. Timer servicing, Context shutdown, signature preservation, and required_cpp rejection before spinning are covered; signal handling remains open.

entries.api: rclpy.spin_once(accelerated_node, timeout_sec=...)
entries.notes: The wrapper delegates to stock execution and reports Python authority. Timer, guard, service, simulated-time, custom executor, callback-exception, signature, and required_cpp fail-before-spin behavior are covered.

entries.api: Custom executors, MultiThreadedExecutor, callback groups, and waitables
entries.notes: A two-thread MultiThreadedExecutor with a reentrant callback group, shutdown, status reporting, and required_cpp rejection is covered. Custom executor subclasses, waitables, and sustained stress remain open.

entries.api: rclpy.task.Future set_result/set_exception/cancel completion
entries.notes: Future completion remains stock-authoritative under every policy to avoid destabilizing executor internals. Result completion, done callbacks, signature preservation, and required_cpp behavior are covered.

entries.api: Node.create_guard_condition/GuardCondition.trigger/destroy_guard_condition
entries.notes: Stock guard-condition identity, callback groups, trigger/dispatch, destruction, compatible status, bounded warnings, signature preservation, and required_cpp rejection before creation are covered.

entries.api: Node.create_service/create_client and service spinning
entries.notes: A local SetBool client/server request, Future response, callback group, discovery, status, identity, and teardown match stock. required_cpp rejects user service/client creation before side effects while preserving constructor-owned services.

entries.api: ActionClient and ActionServer with generated action types: accept, reject, feedback, result, and cancel
entries.notes: Exact stock ActionClient/ActionServer objects, generated types, nodes, custom Context, reentrant groups, and MultiThreadedExecutor semantics remain authoritative. Activated behavior must equal stock for success, rejection, complete feedback, result, cancellation, callback order, and teardown; status reports Python ownership and required_cpp rejects before handle or waitable creation. No C++ action route is claimed.

entries.api: Stock-authoritative Python ActionClient interoperating with an ahead-of-time rclcpp_action server
entries.notes: A generated nested action proves discovery, goal acceptance, feedback, successful result, and teardown against a separately compiled C++ server on local x86-64. The same source proof is wired into native ARM64 CI but is not certified there until a remote run succeeds. The Python client remains explicitly reported as Python-owned.

entries.api: Custom action QoS, explicit goal UUIDs, synchronous calls, abort/error callbacks, concurrent goals, and result expiry
entries.notes: The certified corpus uses explicit callback groups and result_timeout, but custom QoS, UUID injection, synchronous APIs, abort and exception propagation, concurrency stress, and expired-result behavior remain unproven.

entries.api: Local parameter declaration, callbacks, mutation, listing, and parameter-service graph
entries.notes: The stock node remains sole owner. Values, overrides, callbacks, mutation, listing, service graph identity, status, custom Context, and required_cpp rejection before mutation are covered.

entries.api: AsyncParameterClient and remote parameter events
entries.notes: An AsyncParameterClient discovers all six stock services, remotely sets and gets a declared parameter, observes the matching ParameterEvent value, and tears down every client and subscription. The exact stock objects remain authoritative and activated behavior matches the stock corpus.

entries.api: LifecycleNode construction, configure, cleanup, and unconfigured shutdown
entries.notes: The exact stock class, pre-activation subclass, Context, state machine, callbacks, and teardown remain authoritative. Communication-enabled and disabled construction, successful and failed configure callbacks, cleanup, unconfigured shutdown, bounded fallback reporting, signature preservation, and required_cpp rejection before Node initialization are covered.

entries.api: LifecycleNode change_state, get_state, get_available_states, get_available_transitions, and get_transition_graph services
entries.notes: All five stock lifecycle services are discovered and queried in a custom Context. Service-driven activate/deactivate, state responses, transition inventories, callback inputs, and client teardown match the stock application corpus; lifecycle-node status represents their aggregate stock ownership.

entries.api: LifecycleNode.create_lifecycle_publisher and activation-gated publish
entries.notes: The exact stock LifecyclePublisher and managed activation flag remain authoritative. Inactive publishes are suppressed, while active publishes use the existing certified same-handle C++ Publisher.publish route and deliver to a stock subscription; deactivation and destruction match stock.

entries.api: LifecycleNode ERROR callback processing, invalid transitions, and shutdown from active or inactive states
entries.notes: Configure FAILURE and recovery to an unconfigured shutdown are covered, but ERROR/on_error behavior, invalid transition exceptions, and every shutdown origin do not yet have differential evidence.

entries.api: Normal interpreter exit after rclcpp bringup and node creation
entries.notes: Both the native lane and compatible stock-authority scenario return normally without forced exit, leaked graph identity, or teardown fault.

entries.api: Repeated explicit Context init/shutdown cycles while another Context exists
entries.notes: Three sequential custom Contexts each create an exact stock node, complete a same-handle C++ publish to a stock subscription, tear down, and leave the default Context untouched while the corpus Context remains live.

entries.api: Repeated init/shutdown of the default global Context
entries.notes: The explicit-Context matrix does not prove repeated default-global initialization or interactions with the process-global rclcpp bringup Context.

entries.api: C++ message CDR serialization compared with rclpy.serialization
entries.notes: Flat and tested message bytes match the stock serializer; this is a native capability and not yet a global rclpy.serialization patch.
